title: introduce probing replay coordinator and deterministic warmup phase for CUDA graph replays
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We observed two classes of intermittent regressions in CUDA graph capture/replay on production traffic: (1) replays running with kernels chosen for a different shape/sequence regime after autoscaling or dynamic batching, and (2) cold KV cache misses during replay warmup that cause latency spikes and token-accounting regressions. This PR introduces a deterministic replay coordinator plus an explicit probing warmup phase that runs short, bounded probe traces to classify the current execution regime and prepopulate KV cache before allowing full golden-path replay. The design goals were: deterministic behavior across restarts, minimal added tail latency for the probe, and safe rollback to the legacy fallback behavior when probes detect incompatibility.

Summary of changes (single-string): Added a ReplayCoordinator component that sequences: (a) probe generation and execution on a pinned worker, (b) deterministic kernel mapping selection recorded with a small capture manifest, and (c) KV-cache prepopulation hooks that run side-effect-less prefix traces. Introduced a lightweight probe-trace generator that synthesizes 3 short traces representative of common sequence length distributions derived from recent request histograms. New metrics and tracing: replay_probe.duration_ms, replay_probe.outcome, replay_coordinator.state, cudagraph.capture_manifest (hash), and kvcache.prefill_hits. Added end-to-end integration tests that run a deterministic simulated traffic harness to validate replay idempotency and fallback paths. Added a regression test that replays a captured session across an artificial kernel mapping change to ensure the coordinator triggers an immediate safe-fallback.

Files changed (high level): ["runtime/replay/coordinator.cpp", "runtime/replay/probe_runner.cpp", "runtime/replay/capture_manifest.h", "runtime/kv_cache/prefill.cc", "runtime/scheduler/pinned_worker.cc", "tests/integration/replay_probe_harness.cc", "docs/observability/replay_metrics.md", "ci/test_data/replay_samples/*"]

Detailed notes on implementation: The ReplayCoordinator lives inside the serving runtime's replay path and participates only when cudagraphs are enabled for a model. On incoming warmup requests the coordinator first checks for a recent capture_manifest match: if present and checksum matches, we skip probing. Otherwise coordinator schedules up to three probe traces onto a pinned worker (fixed GPU stream) using a short, deterministic schedule (no wall-clock jitter). Probe traces are small prefix inputs that exercise the model's typical branching (long/short token counts) while avoiding external side effects (no writeback to stateful stores). The probe runner records kernel mapping fingerprints: kernel ids + launch config serialized into the capture_manifest. If all probes succeed within configured tight timeouts and kernel fingerprints match expectations, the coordinator invokes the cudagraph capture flow and pre-populates the KV cache by replaying the same probes into the cache warmup path. If a probe fails or mapping mismatch is observed, the coordinator marks the session as INCOMPATIBLE and routes live traffic to fallback path (legacy per-token execution) and emits replay_probe.outcome=failed. To minimize risk, we bound probe work to a single GPU worker and limit retries per minute by default.

Observability and CI: New metrics implemented with tagging by model_id and region. Added a dashboard tile showing probe success rate and average prefill_hits. Unit + integration CI initially flagged a flaky test "ReplayProbeHarness.TimeoutRace" on the first run; I tightened the probe timeout, added an epoch-based probe seed (to remove timer-jitter dependence) and the CI suite passed on re-run. The full CI matrix on main (linux-gcc-14, cuda-13.3) passed; smoke tests on a pinned small GPU in CI were used to avoid noise from shared GPU pools.

Backward-compat & safety: feature gated behind runtime flag "cudagraph_replay_probe" (disabled by default for <=stable-2025.08 customers). All probe activity is non-destructive; KV prefill uses separate, ephemeral keys that are promoted only after successful probe validation. The coordinator emits an event for any fallback decision to help SRE surface regressions quickly.

Release notes: "Added an opt-in deterministic replay coordinator and probing warmup to improve cudagraph capture stability and reduce KV-cache cold-start regressions. Disabled by default; opt-in via runtime flag."

Why this is different from prior work: Prior PRs focused on heuristic warmup thresholds and relaxed shape guards. This change introduces a short, deterministic probing phase and an explicit manifest of kernel mappings to make replay decisions reproducible across restarts and after autoscaling. The manifest plus probe sequence reduces silent regressions where a replay would succeed in capture but fail at replay time due to unexpected kernel scheduling decisions.

review_thread: Arjun: The manifest serialization looks good; one question: how do we prevent the manifest from staling after a kernel update? Consider adding a versioned field in serialization.
Maya: Added versioned manifest header and checksum. If checksum mismatch is detected we explicitly fall back. See capture_manifest.h (version field added).
Noelle: Found a race where probe completion could race with worker reclamation in high churn load; suggested stronger ownership token.
Maya: Applied ownership token and pinned_worker now refuses to evict in-flight probes (see pinned_worker.cc). Added a unit test for eviction-safety.

Diego: CI showed a flaky TimeoutRace; narrowed probe timeout and switched to epoch-based probe seeding to remove nondeterminism from system timers.
